
The J. Paul Getty Museum exhibition: Book of Beasts in 2019, featured a large collection of illuminated bestiaries. Unique about this exhibition, was the focus on the iconic imagery of the represented beasts. Namely, the collection focuses on the anthropomorphic features of the images that it contains. It features animals which enable reflection on human concerns. As such, it includes relevant human emotions and respondent action, giving more insight into the various ways that humans interpret their world than it does give insight into human attitudes toward animals [@morr19].
